hints: Notice the $24 \, \text{V}$ battery drives current only through the $9.0 \, \Omega$ and $3.0 \, \Omega$ series pair when the galvanometer current is zero.
Zero galvanometer current means there is no p.d. between its two terminals, so the e.m.f. of X must equal the p.d. across the resistor it is connected across.
First find the series current from $24 \, \text{V}$ and $12 \, \Omega$, then calculate $V = IR$ for the $3.0 \, \Omega$ resistor.
walkthrough: The left loop has the $24 \, \text{V}$ battery in series with $9.0 \, \Omega$ and $3.0 \, \Omega$. Because the galvanometer reads zero, no current branches to X, so all current stays in this left loop.
Total resistance is $R = 9.0 + 3.0 = 12 \, \Omega$. The current is $I = V/R = 24/12 = 2.0 \, \text{A}$.
Battery X is connected between the bottom wire and, via the galvanometer, the junction of the two resistors. It is therefore balanced against the p.d. across the $3.0 \, \Omega$ resistor.
That p.d. is $V = IR = 2.0 \times 3.0 = 6.0 \, \text{V}$ with the top positive relative to the bottom.
For zero current in the galvanometer there must be zero p.d. across that branch, so e.m.f. of X must equal $6.0 \, \text{V}$. This is option A.

options.A: The p.d. across the $3.0 \, \Omega$ resistor is $6.0 \, \text{V}$, so battery X must be $6.0 \, \text{V}$ for zero p.d. across the galvanometer branch.
options.B: This does not equal the potential divider voltage across the $3.0 \, \Omega$ resistor from the $24 \, \text{V}$ supply.
options.C: This is close to the p.d. across the $9.0 \, \Omega$ resistor, not the $3.0 \, \Omega$ resistor that X is balanced against.
options.D: This is the p.d. across the $9.0 \, \Omega$ resistor, whereas X is connected across the $3.0 \, \Omega$ resistor.
